sections.title: The verb follows the object
sections.content: In Hungarian the verb ending depends on the object. With *egy*, a bare noun or no object, you use the endings you already know. With a definite object, something specific that both speakers know (*a kenyeret*, *az almát*, and next lesson *ezt* and *azt*), the verb takes a different set: the definite endings. Compare *Kérek egy kenyeret.* (any bread) and *Kérem a kenyeret.* (that bread, I'll take it).

sections.title: I-form: any one → the particular one
rows: I ask for → I ask for the ...

sections.title: The definite endings
rows: I, you, he / she ask for the ...
I, you, he / she take the ...
I, you, he / she cook the ...

sections.content: Choose by the object, not by the verb: *egy* or a bare noun means *kérek, veszek, főzök*; *a / az* + noun means *kérem, veszem, főzöm*. In the I-form, verbs such as *eszem* and *iszom* look the same either way.
